archetypes.label: Graph & DB Visualization Platforms
archetypes.description: End-user products/platforms that connect to graph (or graph-shaped) data and visually explore it — MetroGraph's most direct competitive set. Includes graph-DB-native explorers, DB-agnostic enterprise graph-viz platforms, and commercial graph-viz toolkits.

archetypes.label: Database Schema & ERD Modeling
archetypes.description: Tools that visualize, design, and explore database schemas (ERDs, live-DB introspection). Directly competes with MetroGraph's DB-visualization wedge for the noSQL/SQL startup + data-engineer ICP.

archetypes.label: Node-Based UI & Graph Rendering Libraries
archetypes.description: Developer libraries/SDKs for rendering nodes/edges and graphs — the technical foundation layer MetroGraph competes with / could build on (React Flow is the explicit rendering-layer peer). Not product competitors but shape the builder's expectations.

archetypes.label: Graph & Multi-Model Database Engines
archetypes.description: The graph/multi-model DB backends whose data MetroGraph would visualize. Adjacency, not viz competitors — but the source-of-truth layer and a partnership/integration surface. Several bundle their own viz (linked into graph-db-visualization).

archetypes.label: Workflow Automation / iPaaS (node-based)
archetypes.description: Visual node-based workflow/automation and integration platforms. The canonical 'endless folders/panes/configs' HCI-comparison set MetroGraph's metro-map wedge targets.

archetypes.label: Visual RAG / AI-Agent Builders
archetypes.description: No-code/low-code canvas builders for RAG pipelines and AI agents. Directly named in MetroGraph's wedge (agent-builder HCI weak link, agent-vs-graph-chat confusion).

archetypes.label: Low-Code Internal Tools & No-Code Databases
archetypes.description: Internal-tool builders, low-code app platforms, and no-code database/spreadsheet frontends. Wedge target (config sprawl) plus ICP-adjacent data frontends (NocoDB/Teable/Baserow over SQL/noSQL).

archetypes.label: BI, Analytics & Data Notebooks
archetypes.description: Business-intelligence dashboards and analyst notebooks. Adjacent to MetroGraph via the data-engineer/analyst ICP and the 'consumption layer' of the modern data stack; AI-native notebooks (Hex) signal the AI+UI convergence.

archetypes.label: Diagramming & Diagram-as-Code
archetypes.description: General diagramming, whiteboards, and diagram-as-code tools. Adjacent visualization space; several (Mermaid, draw.io, Lucidchart) render ERDs/graphs. Figma/FigJam appears here as a called-out MetroGraph integration partner, not a pure competitor.

archetypes.label: Data Orchestration, ETL/ELT & Observability
archetypes.description: Transformation, ingestion, orchestration, data-quality/observability, and warehouse/lakehouse platforms for the data-engineer ICP. Adjacency (many expose DAG/lineage graph views); establishes the stack MetroGraph plugs into.

pain_themes: UI surface-area bloat & feature sprawl: endless folders/panes/configs/popups, widget overload, 'extremely basic'/'90s movie' interfaces, cognitive overload from low-value features (Retool, UiPath, LaunchDarkly, general SaaS). MetroGraph's core wedge.

Steep learning curve & config complexity in visual/low-code builders: confusing node setup, inadequate JS env, nested conditions/retries/fallbacks pile up; 'mental model takes too long' (n8n, Zapier, Make, OutSystems, Blue Prism, Weaviate modules, Milvus).
Complexity ceiling with no escape hatch: visual builders break when real-world complexity emerges; ~10% of edge cases force users to JS/code hacks; 'hard stop' beyond the toolkit.

Users fleeing the UI for AI chat ('worst of both worlds'): no-code handles the easy 90%, hard cases go to ChatGPT/Claude; apps must meet users inside their AI environment. The category splits into fixed-sequence builders vs. personal AI assistants.

Agent-vs-UI confusion & agent feature creep: agents bolted onto every platform (30+ Slackbot features), unclear when to use agent vs UI; MCP/context bloat (7 servers = 33.7% of context window; 8k+ tokens before the user speaks).

Tool sprawl, fragmentation & vendor lock-in: 5-10 tools per data pipeline; ~$18k/employee in unused licenses; 50%+ orgs consolidating; lock-in (Bubble no source export, ArangoDB Apache→BSL license shift) and costly migrations.

Visualization-only tools under-differentiated & under-funded: Observable (no rounds since 2022) and Azimutt (bootstrapped) signal viz-only struggles to monetize without an orchestration/AI layer; 'market waiting for differentiation'.

Query-language / SQL/Cypher barrier: Looker needs SQL+LookML, Tableau needs LOD mastery, Cypher is hard for newcomers (spawns visual query builders); a barrier for the non-technical exploration MetroGraph targets.

Data-engineering stack fragmentation & operational overhead: Airflow infra complexity/observability/onboarding; modern data stack needs 5+ tools (dbt+Airflow+observability+BI+governance); dbt+Fivetran merger born of fragmentation frustration.

Graph adoption friction: graph DBs face an 'uphill battle for mass adoption'; Neo4j frustration spawns alternatives (Grafeo, FalkorDB, PuppyGraph); historical underutilization despite projected growth — an opening for better HCI.
dropped: Foundation model providers (Anthropic Claude/MCP, OpenAI GPT-5/Operator, Google DeepMind Gemini/ADK, Mistral/Le Chat, Cohere, xAI Grok, DeepSeek, Alibaba Qwen, Meta Llama 4) — LLM providers, not visualization or builder UX; ingest as ecosystem context only.
Inference / GPU compute / model serving (Modal, CoreWeave, Replicate, Baseten, RunPod, BentoML, Groq, Together AI, Fireworks AI) — compute/serving infra, no DB/graph viz UX.

Vector DBs / RAG storage / agent memory (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, Chroma, pgvector, LanceDB, Azure AI Search, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Mem0, Letta, Zep, Cognee) — retrieval infra; no visual UX to tear down (Cognee/Memgraph KG adjacency noted under graph-databases).

notes: Consolidated 7 cartographer outputs (~300+ raw candidates) into a deduplicated master registry of 158 in-scope companies across 10 emergent archetypes. Card-sort produced 10 clusters rather than the suggested 5-8 because the data genuinely spans three distinct competitive rings: (A) DIRECT — graph-db-visualization + db-schema-modeling (these visualize databases/graphs = MetroGraph's wedge; all flagged is_direct_competitor=true, ~29 companies); (B) ADJACENT/FOUNDATIONAL — node-graph-libraries (rendering layer, React Flow is the explicit tech peer), graph-databases (the backends MetroGraph reads + a partnership surface), data-bi-notebook and data-orchestration (the data-engineer ICP's stack, many with DAG/lineage graph views); (C) WEDGE-TARGET UX — workflow-automation, rag-agent-builders, internal-tools-lowcode, diagramming (the 'endless folders/panes/configs/popups' HCI weak link MetroGraph attacks). Dedup highlights: Neo4j, n8n, Azimutt, ChartDB, Prisma Studio, Kuzu, Memgraph, Gephi, Cambridge Intelligence/ReGraph, Tom Sawyer, Linkurious appeared across 3-5 cartographers → single rows; Neo4j/Memgraph/Kuzu/NebulaGraph split into engine row (graph-databases) + viz-product row (graph-db-visualization) since products differ. Figma is filed under diagramming but flagged as a called-out INTEGRATION PARTNER, not a competitor (same for Google Drive, not a discovery hit). Each archetype proposes competitors-<key> and ux-teardown-<key> leaves to scaffold via `pnpm leaf add market/<leaf>`. The `market` domain has schema.market.sql + the algebra tables (companies, products, features, segments, personas, jobs_pains_gains, pricing_*, ux_*, competitors, claims, etc.) ready to receive this registry; no leaves exist yet, so this seeds the corpus. Whitespace signal worth a claim row: no dominant tool combines graph/DB schema visualization + agent-workflow orchestration in a single low-surface-area (metro-map) view — competitors specialize in graph-viz OR workflow OR schema OR notebooks, and viz-only players (Observable, Azimutt) are under-funded.
